title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 26
paragraphs: After Alyattes's death, Croesus, his son, succeeded to the kingdom at the age of thirty-five. He (as I said) waged war against the Hellenes, and the first he attacked were the Ephesians. When the Ephesians were besieged by him, they dedicated their city to Artemis and tied a rope from the temple to the wall of the city — the distance between the old city, then under siege, and the temple being seven furlongs. They, then, were the first on whom Croesus laid hands, but afterwards he did the same to the other Ionian and Aeolian cities one by one, making various complaints against them — serious charges where he could find serious grounds, and trifling ones against others.
